scope: Post-hoc feasibility audit of already archived cases, not independent validation or new network experiments
certificate: Outward rational state intervals, aggregate-addition float32 roundoff bounds, threshold and scheduling guards; stop on first inconclusive guard
rounding: IEEE binary32 round-to-nearest ties-to-even, original operation ordering, no reassociation, no NaN/overflow; finite-state model only
inputs_allowed: Original archived state/spikes; original and candidate graphs; frozen source; external input protocol. Candidate state files are opened only after certification for audit
success: Any fully certified nonzero case is feasibility coverage, not proof of novel theory, transfer or speedup
failure: Inconclusive certificate is not a prediction of spike divergence
cost: Report setup separately; incoming-event count, touched chunks, checked slots and observed local audit times. No comparison of Python times with archived instrumented Rust as speedup
constraints: No simulator launched, no new graphs/inputs, no changes to paper or archived evidence; no tuning of bounds after results
